spec_issues: The held-out set is SNU-FILM-arb (tests/task/pipeline/sources.json: 'primary_benchmark': 'snu-film-arb', 270 intervals, 90 per factor in tests/config.json), i.e. the test lists of a public benchmark built from GoPro test and YouTube footage. The agents are not told; the review rule calls this 'an application of the public validation/test exclusion, not an additional secret rule' (tests/task/review.py:56-58). No trial downloaded SNU-FILM or GoPro test footage (searched all 18 trajectories); three used the GOPRO_Large train split (Gemini 4q3ghq, Astra 4svmql, Astra 35pvsa), which is allowed.

The 300 s per-request ceiling is enforced in grading (tests/config.json 'request_timeout_seconds': 300; tests/task/verifier.py:63; validate.py:73,86-87) although the contract describes it as 'adjustable debugging limits, not benchmark speed requirements' (task.yaml:79-80). It did not obviously cause any zero here, but it contradicts the stated whole-pass-only rule.

The zero anchor is a 'permitted-standalone-RAFT-deterministic-synthesis' baseline and the one anchor is GIMM-VFI-R-P, the forbidden specialist (tests/task/calibration.json baseline_id, target_id). Every one of the 17 scored trials built pretrained standalone flow (RAFT, SEA-RAFT, WAFT or GMFlow) + warping + a learned synthesis net, i.e. the baseline plus a trained refiner. That is consistent with the rules, but the score mostly measures how well an agent trains a refiner on top of the baseline's own flow.
verifier_issues: Each of the six components (LPIPS and FloLPIPS at 4x/8x/16x) is clipped to [0,1] (task.yaml:64-71), so beating GIMM-VFI on one factor cannot offset a shortfall elsewhere and differences near the top (Opus 91.1, Astra 91.2) are compressed. The grade page publishes no per-factor breakdown, only the scalar and hashes.

The three public intervals all come from one portrait 384x720 phone clip (sequence-0027), unlike the mostly 1280x720 GoPro/YouTube held-out footage. Agents who tuned inference on them were misled: Fable 5xwyxm's chosen config scored LPIPS 0.0185/0.0300/0.0599 on public ([148], at or below the target anchor) but 58.2 on held-out.

DeepSeek 1sb7so scored 0 with 'TimeoutError: Sequence request exceeded its deadline' after a selfcheck on the same folder projected 136 s of the 2250 s budget. The grader does not report which request or how long it took.
task_level.noise: Wallet ordering is noisy: Opus 91.1/86.7/87.8, Astra 85.3/91.2/84.6, Fable 78.5/81.8/58.2, Gemini 66.9/47.1/56.5, Muse 68.8/49.8/55.9, DeepSeek 56.8/0/64.2. Only Opus and Astra are clearly separated from the rest. Between those two the winner flips by wallet with margins of 5.8 ($10), 4.5 ($50) and 3.2 ($200) points; near-identical RAFT+refiner recipes elsewhere swing by 20+ points (Fable $50 81.8 vs $200 58.2), so a re-run could plausibly swap Opus and Astra at any wallet. The Opus-or-Astra pair at the top is robust.
task_level.elicitation: Astra (Codex) spent far more model budget ($247-276 per trial, 1,068-1,167 steps) and used larger flow stacks (SEA-RAFT, WAFT, DINOv2/v3, Depth Anything). Opus got 91.1 from $8.10 of 4090 time. DeepSeek hit its context limit repeatedly (3-6 context compactions per trial). Gemini trials were '-r2' re-runs and stopped after 2.6-4 h with most of the wallet unspent. The DeepSeek $50 zero is the only outcome plausibly caused by the setup.
task_level.epoch_rationale: All 18 reviews passed and I found no missed violation (no specialist weights, no SNU-FILM or other test-split use). The one zero (DeepSeek 1sb7so, timeout after a passing selfcheck) is a suspected infrastructure or hidden-gate failure, but that model's other runs score 56.8 and 64.2, far below the $50 winner (Astra 91.2), so no winner changes.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming: every trial trained a flow-warping-plus-refinement interpolator from permitted flow models on public training splits, and the reviewer checked provenance carefully (it caught and cleared Fable 1dybjq's speed-test download of a Vimeo test shard). The scores reflect engineering quality: data choice (OpenVid/Mixkit/Vimeo/GoPro train), joint flow fine-tuning and test-time augmentation. Nothing is plausibly novel; the best runs reimplement softmax-splatting refiners close to published designs.
